author: Brian Didlake
title: Memphis family worries about losing SNAP benefits amid cuts - NewsBreak
text:
By Brian Didlake ,
1 hours ago MEMPHIS, Tenn. — One Memphis man says he is in limbo right now, having to make some tough budgeting decisions and fearful of losing his SNAP benefits.
This comes as the State Department of Human Services says it doesn’t have a confirmed date for partial benefits.
“A word is not putting food on the table, if you’re going to do it, do it, if you’re not, then let us know so we can prepare for it at least,” said Cedric Nesby.
“I can’t budget because I got to spend my utility money on food. You know I can’t let, My son is not ever going to come in this house and say I’m hungry and not going to eat,” said Cedric Nesby.
Council urges lawmakers to expand relief for families amid shutdown It’s been 5 years since WREG last spoke with Nesby.
Then his family received help through WREG’s Pass It On. The year prior, Cedric Junior, Nesby’s son was shot, paralyzing him from the waist down. Cedric Junior was 9 years old at the time.
Since then, Cedric said he has not been able to work because he is the sole caregiver for his son.
He said his son is a bit more mobile now, but says it’s still been difficult to find work.
“It’s killing me, it’s pretty much—I’m pretty sure I am not the only person hurting,” said Nesby.
Cedric said he is set to receive his SNAP benefits in a little more than a week, but says that is up in the air.
Gov. Lee grants $5M to support Tennessee food banks “I don’t know what is going on with SNAP. I don’t know whether we are going to receive them or not,” said Nesby.
Nesby said that he has not received a letter about SNAP benefits, and that he’s relying on the news to be informed.
Tennessee’s Department of Human Services is posting that it does not have a confirmed date for partial benefits.
Last Friday, 2 federal judges ruled the federal government had to at least partially fund the food assistance program.
But with the state saying even when it knows what that amount will be, it will still have to recalculate benefits, leaving some 167,000 Memphis-Shelby County families in limbo.
“People want to have somewhere to go to get help, and then when you go to these places to get help then it’s like ah we got to put you on a waiting plan. That’s not helping, that’s not helping you can’t put nobody on a waiting list that needs help now,” said Nesby.
“We can only do the best we can, we can only do the best we can,” said Nesby.
Governor Lee has said he’ll be sending $5 million in state funding to food banks to help carry the burden, and the city of Memphis is chipping in another 500-grand.
The city and the county are also asking the governor to pause the state tax on groceries and asking MGLW to pause disconnections.
